proof_summary: Since the product is not \(1\), the finite associated-prime set is nonempty and therefore has a maximum \(m\). Membership makes \(m\) prime, while any prime divisor \(q\le\sqrt{2n-m}\le\sqrt{2n}\) witnessing that \(2n-m\) is composite would imply \(m\equiv 2n\pmod q\), contradicting the defining modular exclusion; hence the complement is prime and the two terms sum to \(2n\).
